Review SoWork?

Reviewers mostly say SoWork makes remote work feel more social and natural, with avatars, spatial audio, and virtual offices helping recreate casual, spontaneous conversations that standard video tools miss. Many also like having chat, video, and AI meeting summaries in one place, saying it reduces tool switching and supports smoother collaboration, especially for fully remote teams. The playful design and customization are often seen as good for team connection. Main drawbacks mentioned are heavier performance on older laptops, some setup quirks, and one sharp complaint about a mid-subscription guest access policy change.

# SoWork: The Glow-Up Edition - All-in-one virtual HQ for high-performing remote teams

by

Cursor

•

Since our 2023 launch, SoWork’s had a massive glow-up: lightning-fast performance, a sleek new UI/UX, fully-featured mobile apps, fun built-in games, and dozens of upgrades based on your feedback. It’s everything remote work should be. Finally.

### Replies

Report [...] 🎨 Thousands more avatar and office customization options  
🤙🏽 Dozens of upgrades driven by user feedback  
  
If you don’t know us yet, SoWork is the virtual HQ for remote teams. Think: spatial video, async collab tools, and AI productivity tools built-in, all designed to make teamwork feel as natural and spontaneous as being together in real life.  
  
Our users told us what was and wasn’t working. So we went heads down and built what they asked for, so we could close basically ALL the gaps that SoWork 1.0 had (and there were lots!).  
  
If you’ve ever felt disconnected working remotely, or tired of hopping between Zoom, Slack, and your calendar just to talk to your team and ship stuff, SoWork might be the game-changer you’ve been waiting for.
